VS Code/Cursor extension host fetches dropper from nrwl/nx orphan commit on GitHub AIInstallation Medium
The compromised Nx Console v18.95.0 pulled a 498 KB obfuscated dropper hidden in an orphan (dangling) commit on the legitimate nrwl/nx GitHub repository. This UC hunts VS Code / Cursor / their Node extension-host processes contacting raw.githubusercontent.com or codeload.github.com on nrwl/nx paths — a request shape that the legitimate Nx Console does not make at runtime. Rationale: Anchors on the article's explicit claim that the 498 KB dropper was hidden in an orphan commit of the legitimate nrwl/nx GitHub repository — a request the unmodified Nx Console extension does not make. Pairs the VS Code / Cursor / extension-host process identity with the unique nrwl/nx GitHub raw/codeload/blob API paths. Cross-checked against GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w and StepSecurity which confirm the orphan-commit dropper mechanism. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1105 T1102.001
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer working on the Nx project clones nrwl/nx via VS Code's built-in git integration (path will be /git/refs or /info/refs, not /blobs)
  • VS Code extension recommendation lookup that hits api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx (low-bytes metadata read, not the blob/tree paths)
  • Nx CLI itself fetching update manifests from raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx/<release-tag>/ paths
  • Renovate/Dependabot bot acting via the extension host
Suppression filter
| where not (RemoteUrl has_any ("/git/refs","/git/info","/releases/download/")) and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("renovate","dependabot","semantic-release"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the URL path was a /git/blobs/<sha>, /git/trees/<sha>, or raw URL on a commit hash not present in nrwl/nx's tagged release tree — orphan commits return blobs but aren't reachable from any branch tip. Capture response size; the legitimate use-cases are KB-scale, the dropper was ~498 KB. 2) Contain: isolate the developer endpoint, treat as UC1-confirmed and run the UC1 hashes against DeviceFileEvents. 3) Hunt: extract the commit SHA from RemoteUrl and search the rest of the fleet for the same SHA — the same orphan blob would be fetched by every infected install. Also pivot to DNS for github.com/<unknown-actor-owned>/<repo>/issues which the payload uses as a dead-drop.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","node.exe","code-insiders.exe","codium.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper")
   or InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("code.exe","cursor.exe","code-insiders.exe")
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx/","codeload.github.com/nrwl/nx/","api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/blobs","api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/trees")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where Url has_any ("raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx/","codeload.github.com/nrwl/nx/","api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/blobs","api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/trees")
   or HttpHostName in~ ("raw.githubusercontent.com","codeload.github.com") and UrlOriginal has "nrwl/nx"
| where SrcUsername != "" and (HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent has_any ("VSCode","vscode","Cursor","node-fetch","axios","got","undici") or DvcHostname != "")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcUsername, Url, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpResponseBodyBytes
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: VS Code/Cursor Extension Host Fetches nrwl/nx Orphan-Commit Dropper
id: c47e8b95-2a13-4f08-b1d6-7c5e9f3a6e72
description: Detects Code.exe, Cursor.exe or their Node extension host contacting GitHub paths under nrwl/nx (raw, codeload, blob/tree APIs) — the dropper path used by the May 2026 Nx Console v18.95.0 compromise.
references:
    - https://www.aikido.dev/blog/vs-code-extension-github-breach
    - https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
    - attack.t1105
    - attack.t1102.001
    - attack.command_and_control
logsource:
    category: network_connection
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_process:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\Code.exe'
            - '\Cursor.exe'
            - '\node.exe'
            - '\Code - Insiders.exe'
            - '\codium.exe'
    selection_destination:
        DestinationHostname|contains:
            - 'raw.githubusercontent.com'

| join({#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 | ContextImageFileName=/(Code|Cursor|node)\.?(exe)?$/i}, field=[aid, ContextProcessId], include=[RemoteAddressIP4, RemotePort])
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, DomainName], function=count())

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Web where (Web.url IN ("*raw.githubusercontent.com/nrwl/nx/*","*codeload.github.com/nrwl/nx/*","*api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/blobs/*","*api.github.com/repos/nrwl/nx/git/trees/*")) AND Web.src_app IN ("code.exe","cursor.exe","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)") by host Web.dest Web.url Web.src_app Web.user Web.bytes_in | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where bytes_in > 100000 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

macOS Python backdoor persistence via kitty-monitor LaunchAgent and cat.py drop AIInstallation High
After execution, the poisoned Nx Console payload drops a Python backdoor on macOS at ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py and registers a LaunchAgent at ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist plus the state file /var/tmp/.gh_update_state. The backdoor uses the GitHub Search API as a dead-drop resolver for follow-on commands. This UC alerts on file creation of any of these named artifacts. Rationale: Anchors on three specific filesystem artifacts disclosed in the GitHub Security Advisory GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w and corroborated by StepSecurity / The Hacker News: the kitty-monitor LaunchAgent (T1543.001 macOS persistence), the cat.py Python dropper under ~/.local/share/kitty/, and the /var/tmp/.gh_update_state semaphore. None of these names belong to any legitimate kitty terminal install (which doesn't write LaunchAgents under com.user.*). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1543.001 T1102.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher staging the IOC for sandbox analysis on a corporate Mac
  • Defender / CrowdStrike quarantine event re-writing the artifact name into the file path
  • Forensic-image restoration of a previously infected machine in a lab VM
  • User experimenting with the legitimate Kitty terminal — note this uses ~/.config/kitty/, not ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("mdworker","mdworker_shared","backupd","Time Machine") and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "com.apple.backupd")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the writing process is python3, node, sh/zsh, or VS Code helper. Identify the GitHub / npm / AWS / Claude credentials accessible to the user on that Mac and the install timestamp of nrwl.angular-console-18.95.0. 2) Contain: kill any python process executing cat.py, unload the LaunchAgent (launchctl unload ~/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist), delete the four artifacts, isolate the endpoint, and immediately rotate all reachable credentials (GitHub PATs, SSH keys, npm tokens, AWS keys, ~/.claude tokens, .env secrets). 3) Hunt: pivot to UC4 (python __DAEMONIZED=1 process), pull the user's GitHub audit log for repo creations / token usage in the window since installation, and search the rest of the macOS fleet for any of these four paths.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where (FolderPath endswith "/.local/share/kitty/cat.py")
   or (FolderPath endswith "/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist")
   or (FolderPath == "/var/tmp/.gh_update_state")
   or (FolderPath startswith "/tmp/kitty-")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where (TargetFilePath endswith "/.local/share/kitty/cat.py")
   or (TargetFilePath endswith "/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist")
   or (TargetFilePath == "/var/tmp/.gh_update_state")
   or (TargetFilePath startswith "/tmp/kitty-")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Nx Console Compromise - macOS Python Backdoor Persistence Artifacts
id: d3f9a7c2-6e4b-4a91-8d72-9f1c5b8e2a3d
description: Detects on-disk landing of the kitty-monitor LaunchAgent, cat.py Python backdoor, or /var/tmp/.gh_update_state state file dropped by the compromised Nx Console v18.95.0 VS Code extension.
references:
    - https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w
    - https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised
    - https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html

detection:

| (TargetFileName=/\/\.local\/share\/kitty\/cat\.py$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/Library\/LaunchAgents\/com\.user\.kitty-monitor\.plist$/i OR TargetFileName=/^\/var\/tmp\/\.gh_update_state$/i OR TargetFileName=/^\/tmp\/kitty-/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName, ContextImageFileName, ContextProcessId], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.file_path IN ("*/.local/share/kitty/cat.py","*/Library/LaunchAgents/com.user.kitty-monitor.plist","/var/tmp/.gh_update_state","/tmp/kitty-*") by host Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_path Filesystem.user | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

Python backdoor self-daemonisation via __DAEMONIZED=1 spawned by VS Code helper or node AIInstallation Medium
The Nx Console v18.95.0 macOS backdoor re-execs itself with __DAEMONIZED=1 in its environment to detach from the VS Code extension host parent — a distinctive marker used by cat.py. This UC hunts python processes spawned by code/cursor/node/shell parents that either run cat.py from the kitty directory or carry the __DAEMONIZED=1 token in their command-line / parent command-line. Rationale: The __DAEMONIZED=1 environment-variable self-relaunch is a distinctive marker called out by the GitHub Security Advisory and StepSecurity writeup for the cat.py backdoor — legitimate Python tooling does not use this sentinel. Combining it with the kitty/cat.py path and a VS Code helper / node / shell parent yields high fidelity. Cross-checked against GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w and StepSecurity IOC list. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html
ATT&CKT1059.006 T1564.012 T1036.005
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • IR analyst replaying a captured payload in a contained VM for triage
  • Detonation sandbox (e.g. ANY.RUN, Joe Sandbox) ingesting the same artifact into corp telemetry
  • Custom DevOps tooling that coincidentally names a script 'cat.py' under a kitty/ subdir (rare — combined with __DAEMONIZED gate this is near-zero)
  • Developer auditing the IOC interactively under their VS Code terminal
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "jupyter" and ProcessCommandLine !has "pytest" and not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("vscode-python","ms-python.python","debugpy"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the full process tree (parent, grandparent), the user, and any open network connections / DNS queries from this PID (pivot to UC2 / DnsRequest). Confirm whether ~/.local/share/kitty/cat.py and the kitty-monitor LaunchAgent exist on disk. 2) Contain: kill the python process (and any children), unload the LaunchAgent, delete the artifacts, isolate the endpoint from the network, and rotate every credential reachable from the box including GitHub PATs, SSH keys, npm/AWS/Claude tokens, and .env secrets. 3) Hunt: extract the contacted GitHub Search API query strings from process arguments (used as dead-drop resolver), then sweep the fleet for the same query patterns and for any new repos in the user's GitHub created during/after the install window.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("python","python3","python3.9","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12","python.exe")

title: Nx Console Compromise - Python cat.py Daemon Spawned by Code Helper or Node

description: Detects the Python backdoor cat.py (or its __DAEMONIZED=1 self-relaunch) launched by a VS Code helper, Cursor helper, node or shell parent. Specific to the May 2026 Nx Console v18.95.0 supply-chain compromise.
references:
    - https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w

    selection_python:

VS Code extension host fan-out reads of developer secrets (.ssh, .aws, .npmrc, ~/.claude/settings.json) AIActions on Objectives Medium
The poisoned Nx Console payload sweeps developer credentials from a fixed list — SSH private keys, AWS credentials, npm tokens, Claude Code config (~/.claude/settings.json — believed to be the first supply-chain payload to target an AI assistant config), gcloud, kube, gnupg, docker, and .env files. This UC alerts when the VS Code / Cursor extension-host Node process touches ≥4 distinct credential-bearing paths within a 10-minute window — a shape no legitimate extension exhibits. Rationale: Anchors on the exact credential-file list disclosed by the GitHub Security Advisory and StepSecurity for the cat.py / Nx Console payload, including the novel target ~/.claude/settings.json that the article calls out as one of the first AI-assistant config harvest behaviours seen in the wild. The ≥4-distinct-paths threshold within 10 minutes is a sweep marker that no legitimate VS Code extension exhibits. Cross-checked GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w + StepSecurity + The Hacker News. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/compromised-nx-console-18950-targeted.html • https://cybersecuritynews.com/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1552.004 T1083
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Git Credential Manager / gh CLI extension legitimately reading ~/.aws/credentials + ~/.npmrc + ~/.ssh/config during repo clone or push
  • Backup software (Time Machine, restic, borg) snapshotting the entire home directory in one pass
  • SAST/SCA scanners (Snyk, Semgrep, Trufflehog) integrated into VS Code performing a workspace secrets scan
  • Initial workstation provisioning script reading dotfiles for migration
  • Cloud-init or dotfiles-bootstrap tooling running once after a fresh checkout
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("git-credential-manager","gh.exe","gh","snyk","semgrep","trufflehog","gitleaks","restic","borg","tmutil","backupd") or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("vscode-snyk","semgrep-ls","gitlens","github.vscode-pull-request-github"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the initiating process is the VS Code extension host (node / Code Helper) and not a known credential manager / SAST scanner / backup tool. Pull DeviceFileEvents for the same host within the prior 30 min for the UC1 hashes or UC3 macOS artifacts. 2) Contain: isolate the endpoint and rotate every credential whose path was hit — at minimum GitHub PATs, all SSH keys, AWS access keys, npm tokens, Anthropic/Claude API keys, gcloud refresh tokens, kubeconfig contexts, and every .env reachable. Force a re-clone-from-scratch of any repo where the .env was read. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC2 (orphan-commit dropper) and UC4 (cat.py daemon) on the same host. Sweep GitHub audit logs for the user's account for repo creations, PAT usage from unfamiliar IPs, and any branch pushes during the install window. Search the npm registry for any packages published by the user's npm account in the same window.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileAccessed","FileRead","FileOpened")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("node","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper","Cursor","Code","code.exe","cursor.exe","python","python3")
| where (FolderPath has_any ("/.ssh/","/.aws/","/.config/gcloud/","/.kube/","/.docker/","/.gnupg/","/.claude/")
     or FileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","id_ecdsa","credentials","known_hosts","authorized_keys",".npmrc","settings.json","config.json")
     or FileName =~ ".env" or FileName startswith ".env." or FolderPath has "/.npmrc")
| where not (FolderPath has "/.claude/" and FileName != "settings.json")    // narrow .claude noise — only the settings.json file matters
| summarize PathCount = dcount(strcat(FolderPath, FileName)),
            Paths = make_set(strcat(FolderPath, FileName), 25),
            FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp)
            by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, bin(Timestamp, 10m)
| where PathCount >= 4    // 4 = sweep threshold; one-off .env read is normal dev work, ≥4 distinct cred files in 10 min is harvesting behaviour
| order by FirstSeen desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("node","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper","Cursor","Code","code.exe","cursor.exe","python","python3")
| where (TargetFilePath has_any ("/.ssh/","/.aws/","/.config/gcloud/","/.kube/","/.docker/","/.gnupg/","/.claude/")
     or TargetFileName in~ ("id_rsa","id_ed25519","id_ecdsa","credentials","known_hosts","authorized_keys",".npmrc")
     or TargetFileName =~ ".env" or TargetFileName startswith ".env."
     or (TargetFilePath has "/.claude/" and TargetFileName =~ "settings.json"))
| summarize PathCount = dcount(TargetFilePath),
            Paths = make_set(TargetFilePath, 25),
            FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated)
            by DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| where PathCount >= 4    // 4 = empirical sweep threshold
| order by FirstSeen desc
source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon) (@process.name:(node OR python OR python3) OR @Image:(*\\node.exe OR *Code\ Helper* OR *cursor-helper* OR *\\Code.exe OR *\\Cursor.exe)) (@file.path:(*/.ssh/id_rsa OR */.ssh/id_ed25519 OR */.ssh/id_ecdsa OR */.aws/credentials OR */.aws/config OR */.npmrc OR */.config/gcloud/* OR */.kube/config OR */.docker/config.json OR */.gnupg/* OR */.claude/settings.json OR */.env OR */.env.*) OR @TargetFilename:(*\\.ssh\\id_rsa OR *\\.aws\\credentials OR *\\.npmrc OR *\\.claude\\settings.json OR *\\.env))
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo ContextImageFileName=/(node|Code Helper|cursor-helper|Cursor|Code|python3?)\.?(exe)?$/i
| (TargetFileName=/\/\.ssh\/(id_(rsa|ed25519|ecdsa)|known_hosts|config|authorized_keys)$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.aws\/(credentials|config)$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.npmrc$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.config\/gcloud\//i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.kube\/config$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.docker\/config\.json$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.gnupg\//i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.claude\/settings\.json$/i OR TargetFileName=/\/\.env(\.[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)?$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, bucket(span=10m)], function=[count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=PathCount), collect(TargetFileName, multival=true)])
| PathCount >= 4

| tstats `summariesonly` count dc(Filesystem.file_path) as distinct_paths values(Filesystem.file_path) as paths min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path IN ("*/.ssh/id_rsa","*/.ssh/id_ed25519","*/.ssh/id_ecdsa","*/.ssh/known_hosts","*/.ssh/config","*/.aws/credentials","*/.aws/config","*/.npmrc","*/.config/gcloud/*","*/.kube/config","*/.docker/config.json","*/.gnupg/*","*/.claude/settings.json","*/.env","*/.env.*")) AND Filesystem.process_name IN ("node","node.exe","Code Helper","Code Helper (Plugin)","cursor-helper","Cursor","Code","python","python3") by host Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name span=10m | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | where distinct_paths >= 4 | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent

| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")

          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'

            - '\chrome.exe'

            - '\firefox.exe'

    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser

level: high

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"

        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities

| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB

| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

status: experimental

    .WebClient.DownloadString — combinations indicating evasion.

    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Tracking TamperedChef Clusters via Certificate and Code Reuse

Unit 42 (Palo Alto)
2026-05-20 13 use cases 8 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Unit 42 analyzes TamperedChef malware clusters that use trojanized productivity apps and malvertising to deliver stealthy payloads to targets. The post Tracking TamperedChef Clusters via Certificate and Code Reuse appeared first on Unit 42 .

ATT&CKT1027 T1053.005 T1176 T1190 T1204.002 T1547.001 T1555.003 T1649
Domainscrystalpdf.com vault.appsuites.ai pdf-tool.appsuites.ai appsuites.ai freeonlinetools.info
Click any ATT&CK pill below to open it on the Matrix
Phase 1
Reconnaissance
Detected
Phase 2
Weaponization
—
Phase 3
Delivery
Detected

Exploitation
Detected

Detected

Detected

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · PowerShell encoded / obfuscated command · Article-specific behavioural hunt — Tracking TamperedChef Clusters via Certificate and Code Reuse
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] TamperedChef shell-company code-signing certificate execution (CL-UNK-1090) · [LLM] TamperedChef trojanized-app activation via --cm / --enableupdate / --fullupdate flags · [LLM] TamperedChef scheduled-task persistence via task.xml + obfuscated JS (appsuite-print.js) · Suspicious browser extension installation · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] TamperedChef C2 / distribution callback to appsuites.ai and sibling domains · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
TamperedChef shell-company code-signing certificate execution (CL-UNK-1090) AIInstallation High
Hunts execution of binaries signed by the five disposable LLCs Unit 42 attributes to the CL-UNK-1090 TamperedChef cluster: CANDY TECH LTD, G.R.CIGAR. LTD, TAU CENTAURI LTD, AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD, METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC. These shell entities exist solely to obtain Authenticode certs for trojanized PDF/recipe/calendar productivity apps; legitimate software from these company names does not exist. Rationale: The five LLC signer strings come directly from the Unit 42 table mapping CL-UNK-1090 binaries to their shell-company signers. These names are unique to the cluster and don't appear in legitimate software publishers. Confirmed against Sophos and WithSecure reporting that the operators rotate cert-issuing LLCs. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course • https://labs.withsecure.com/publications/tamperedchef • https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/cooking-up-trouble-how-tamperedchef-uses-signed-apps-to-deliver-stealthy-payloads/
ATT&CKT1588.003 T1036.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Cert revocation lag — endpoint still running an old TamperedChef sample after the publisher reused the name for benign software (unlikely given the disposable-LLC pattern)
  • Security research VM intentionally running TamperedChef samples for analysis
  • Red team / purple team replaying TamperedChef samples in a lab segment
  • An unrelated company genuinely named G.R.CIGAR LTD shipping legitimate cigar-retail software (verify via SHA256 reputation)
Suppression filter
and not (FolderPath has_any ("\\Windows Defender\\Platform\\", "\\security_research\\", "\\malware_analysis\\"))
Response runbook
Triage: pull SHA256, full path and parent process for every hit; check VT/MISP and any internal IOC list — TamperedChef samples typically score 5-15/70 on VT for first 2 weeks. Contain: isolate the host via Defender Live Response; revoke the user's browser-saved-credential refresh tokens (DPAPI vault is the primary loot target); kill the running PID. Hunt: pivot on the same SHA256 across the fleet (`DeviceProcessEvents | where SHA256 == "<hash>"`), then run UC2 (domain callback) over the prior 60d on every device that ran a signed-by-this-publisher binary — dormancy can be weeks. File for cert revocation request with the issuing CA.
let TamperedChefSigners = dynamic(["CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
   or InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
          Signer = coalesce(ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName),
          Product = ProcessVersionInfoProductName,
          ProcessCommandLine,
          ParentFileName = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let TamperedChefSigners = dynamic(["CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where ActingProcessFileCompany in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
   or ParentProcessFileCompany in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine,
          Signer = coalesce(ActingProcessFileCompany, ParentProcessFileCompany),
          Product = ActingProcessFileProduct,
          SHA256, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TamperedChef Shell-Company Code-Signing Certificate Execution
id: 4a1c6d8e-2b4f-4a8b-9e3a-5f1a2b3c4d5e
description: Detects execution of binaries signed by the disposable LLCs Unit 42 ties to the TamperedChef CL-UNK-1090 cluster (CANDY TECH, G.R.CIGAR, TAU CENTAURI, AMARYLLIS SIGNAL, METROPOLITAN DESIGN).
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tracking-tampered-chef-clusters/
  - https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1588.003
  - attack.t1036.001
  - attack.t1204.002
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    Company:
      - 'CANDY TECH LTD'
      - 'G.R.CIGAR. LTD'
      - 'G.R.CIGAR LTD'
      - 'TAU CENTAURI LTD'
      - 'AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD'
      - 'METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC'
  condition: selection
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Company:"CANDY TECH LTD" OR @Company:"G.R.CIGAR. LTD" OR @Company:"G.R.CIGAR LTD" OR @Company:"TAU CENTAURI LTD" OR @Company:"AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD" OR @Company:"METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC")
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| regex("(CANDY TECH LTD|G\\.R\\.CIGAR\\.? LTD|TAU CENTAURI LTD|AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD|METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC)", field=CompanyName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CompanyName, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_hash) as hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_signature_publisher IN ("CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process_signature_publisher | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@d")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.process_hash) as hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_signature_publisher IN ("CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process_signature_publisher | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@d")
TamperedChef C2 / distribution callback to appsuites.ai and sibling domains AICommand & Control High
Hunts host network egress and DNS to the article's named TamperedChef infrastructure: appsuites.ai (including pdf-tool / vault subdomains), crystalpdf.com, freeonlinetools.info. These are the trojanized-installer download hosts and the dormant-then-activate C2 used by CL-CRI-1089 / CL-UNK-1090. Rationale: appsuites.ai, pdf-tool.appsuites.ai, vault.appsuites.ai, crystalpdf.com and freeonlinetools.info are the article's named distribution/C2 hosts; fullpdf.com added from Sophos corroboration. These are unique campaign-specific domains — no legitimate business overlap. Any callback after the dormancy window is high-confidence post-install activation. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course • https://thehackernews.com/2025/08/tamperedchef-malware-disguised-as-fake.html • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/tamperedchef-infostealer-delivered-through-fraudulent-pdf-editor/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568 T1105
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher manually browsing the campaign sites for analysis — flag once, then add researcher device to allowlist
  • Threat-intel platform sandbox fetching the domains for enrichment (e.g. VT, ANY.RUN) — exclude by source IP range
  • Web-proxy product re-fetching for category lookup — exclude by InitiatingProcessFileName (e.g. ZScalerClient.exe)
  • User clicking a malvertised search result but the install never completes — still high-fidelity since the lure is malicious
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--load-extension","--remote-debugging-port"))
Response runbook
Triage: identify the process that initiated the connection — InitiatingProcessFileName + CompanyName tells you which trojanized app is on the host (AppSuite PDF / CrystalPDF / etc.). Pull the SHA256 and confirm against UC1 signers. Contain: isolate the host; force-revoke the user's browser refresh tokens (Edge/Chrome) and rotate any SSO password since DPAPI vault dump is the stealer's primary objective; uninstall the offending app and remove the scheduled-task persistence (see UC3 / UC4). Hunt: extend the DNS query backwards 90 days for the same domains — install can predate activation by weeks. Run UC1 across the fleet to catch dormant peers with the same signer.
let TamperedChefHosts = dynamic(["appsuites.ai","pdf-tool.appsuites.ai","vault.appsuites.ai","crystalpdf.com","freeonlinetools.info","fullpdf.com"]);
let NetHits = DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where isnotempty(RemoteUrl)
  | extend Host = tolower(tostring(parse_url(RemoteUrl).Host))
  | where Host in~ (TamperedChefHosts) or Host endswith ".appsuites.ai" or Host endswith ".crystalpdf.com"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source = "Network", Indicator = RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName;
let DnsHits = DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
  | extend Query = tolower(tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).DnsQueryString))
  | where Query in~ (TamperedChefHosts) or Query endswith ".appsuites.ai" or Query endswith ".crystalpdf.com"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, Source = "DNS", Indicator = Query, RemoteIP = tostring(parse_json(AdditionalFields).IPAddresses), InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName;
union NetHits, DnsHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let TamperedChefHosts = dynamic(["appsuites.ai","pdf-tool.appsuites.ai","vault.appsuites.ai","crystalpdf.com","freeonlinetools.info","fullpdf.com"]);
ImDnsActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where DnsQuery in~ (TamperedChefHosts) or DnsQuery endswith ".appsuites.ai" or DnsQuery endswith ".crystalpdf.com"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, EventVendor, EventProduct
| union (
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
    | where RequestURL has_any (TamperedChefHosts) or DestinationHostName has_any (TamperedChefHosts)
    | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname = SourceHostName, SrcIpAddr = SourceIP, SrcUsername = SourceUserName, DnsQuery = coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), EventVendor = DeviceVendor, EventProduct = DeviceProduct
  )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

TamperedChef trojanized-app activation via --cm / --enableupdate / --fullupdate flags AIInstallation High
Hunts the article's productivity-app installers (AppSuite, CrystalPDF, Calendaromatic, JustAskJacky) re-launching themselves with the activation flags --cm, --install, --enableupdate or --fullupdate. These flags are the documented switch from dormant-installed state to active stealer/C2 behaviour and have no legitimate productivity-software analogue. Rationale: Article names AppSuite PDF, Calendaromatic, JustAskJacky and CrystalPDF as the trojanized productivity apps. Sophos/Acronis/SecurityOnline corroborate --cm as the documented activation argument and --enableupdate / --fullupdate / --install as the persistent-update flags; these strings don't appear in legitimate productivity-app installers and pair directly with the article's family. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course • https://securityonline.info/tamperedchef-malware-rises-deceptive-apps-use-signed-binaries-and-seo-poisoning-to-hijack-browsers/ • https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/cooking-up-trouble-how-tamperedchef-uses-signed-apps-to-deliver-stealthy-payloads/
ATT&CKT1059 T1204.002 T1480
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Electron-based PDF tool with overlapping product name but different signer — verify against UC1 publisher list
  • Internal app-packaging team testing software-deployment scripts that re-use the --install flag literal — exclude by deployment-server device group
  • Malware-analysis sandbox detonating TamperedChef samples for research
  • User clean-install with legitimate --install on a same-named but unrelated tool — rare given the campaign-specific product names
Suppression filter
and not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msiexec.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "REINSTALL")
Response runbook
Triage: confirm the binary signer matches one of the five shell-company publishers from UC1 — if so, this is the dormant-to-active activation moment. Pull the SHA256, full command line (especially the --cm payload if present), and parent process. Contain: kill the activated process, isolate the host, force-revoke the user's browser-saved-cred refresh tokens and Microsoft 365 sessions (stealer-stage targets DPAPI vault and cookies). Hunt: across the fleet for the same product name regardless of cmdline (UC1 / signer hunt) — those are the dormant peers. Pull DeviceFileEvents for files written by this PID to identify the dropped stealer module.
let TamperedChefBinaries = dynamic(["AppSuitePDF.exe","AppSuite.exe","CrystalPDF.exe","Calendaromatic.exe","JustAskJacky.exe","PDFEditor.exe","ManualFinder.exe","RecipeLister.exe","OneStart.exe","EpiBrowser.exe"]);
let TamperedChefSigners = dynamic(["CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ (TamperedChefBinaries)
   or ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
   or ProcessVersionInfoProductName has_any ("AppSuite","CrystalPDF","Calendaromatic","JustAskJacky","Recipe Lister","Manual Finder")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("--cm ","--cm=","--enableupdate","--fullupdate","--install ")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
          Signer = ProcessVersionInfoCompanyName,
          Product = ProcessVersionInfoProductName,
          ParentFileName = InitiatingProcessFileName,
          ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
let TamperedChefBinaries = dynamic(["AppSuitePDF.exe","AppSuite.exe","CrystalPDF.exe","Calendaromatic.exe","JustAskJacky.exe","PDFEditor.exe","ManualFinder.exe","RecipeLister.exe","OneStart.exe","EpiBrowser.exe"]);
let TamperedChefSigners = dynamic(["CANDY TECH LTD","G.R.CIGAR. LTD","G.R.CIGAR LTD","TAU CENTAURI LTD","AMARYLLIS SIGNAL LTD","METROPOLITAN DESIGN LLC"]);
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where tostring(ActingProcessName) in~ (TamperedChefBinaries)
   or ActingProcessFileCompany in~ (TamperedChefSigners)
   or ActingProcessFileProduct has_any ("AppSuite","CrystalPDF","Calendaromatic","JustAskJacky","Recipe Lister","Manual Finder")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--cm ","--cm=","--enableupdate","--fullupdate","--install ")
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
          Signer = ActingProcessFileCompany,
          Product = ActingProcessFileProduct,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: TamperedChef Productivity-App Activation Flags
id: 6c3e8a2d-4d6b-4cad-bf5c-7b3c4d5e6f7a
description: Detects TamperedChef trojanized productivity apps (AppSuite, CrystalPDF, Calendaromatic, JustAskJacky) launching with documented activation/update flags --cm, --enableupdate, --fullupdate, --install.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/tracking-tampered-chef-clusters/
  - https://securityonline.info/tamperedchef-malware-rises-deceptive-apps-use-signed-binaries-and-seo-poisoning-to-hijack-browsers/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/05/20
tags:
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.t1204.002
  - attack.t1480
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_image:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\AppSuitePDF.exe'
      - '\AppSuite.exe'
      - '\CrystalPDF.exe'
      - '\Calendaromatic.exe'
      - '\JustAskJacky.exe'
      - '\PDFEditor.exe'
      - '\ManualFinder.exe'
      - '\RecipeLister.exe'
  selection_flags:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - '--cm '
      - '--cm='
      - '--enableupdate'
      - '--fullupdate'
      - '--install '
  condition: selection_image and selection_flags
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\AppSuite*.exe OR *\\CrystalPDF.exe OR *\\Calendaromatic.exe OR *\\JustAskJacky.exe OR *\\appsuite*.exe OR *\\crystalpdf.exe OR *\\calendaromatic.exe OR *\\justaskjacky.exe)) (@CommandLine:*--cm* OR @CommandLine:*--enableupdate* OR @CommandLine:*--fullupdate* OR @CommandLine:*--install*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(AppSuite(PDF)?|CrystalPDF|Calendaromatic|JustAskJacky|PDFEditor|ManualFinder|RecipeLister)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/(--cm[=\s]|--enableupdate|--fullupdate|--install\s)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.process_hash) as hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("AppSuitePDF.exe","CrystalPDF.exe","Calendaromatic.exe","JustAskJacky.exe","PDFEditor.exe","ManualFinder.exe","RecipeLister.exe") OR Processes.process LIKE "%AppSuite%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%CrystalPDF%") AND (Processes.process LIKE "%--cm %" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--cm\"%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--enableupdate%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--fullupdate%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--install %") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@d")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent values(Processes.process_hash) as hash from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("AppSuitePDF.exe","CrystalPDF.exe","Calendaromatic.exe","JustAskJacky.exe","PDFEditor.exe","ManualFinder.exe","RecipeLister.exe") OR Processes.process LIKE "%AppSuite%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%CrystalPDF%") AND (Processes.process LIKE "%--cm %" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--cm\"%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--enableupdate%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--fullupdate%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%--install %") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@d")
TamperedChef scheduled-task persistence via task.xml + obfuscated JS (appsuite-print.js) AIInstallation High
Hunts the article-corroborated TamperedChef persistence pattern: schtasks.exe importing a freshly-dropped task.xml that registers a recurring task launching wscript/cscript against an obfuscated JS such as appsuite-print.js. Combines the file-drop, the schtasks /create /xml import and the resulting script-host execution to catch the persistence handoff. Rationale: task.xml drop + schtasks /create /xml + obfuscated JS (appsuite-print.js) is the TamperedChef persistence handoff documented by SecurityOnline and Acronis corroborating the article's CL-CRI-1089 trojanized-app behaviour. The 24h join window catches the schedule registration paired to the subsequent script-host launch, dramatically reducing FP vs schtasks alone. Cross-checked against: • https://securityonline.info/tamperedchef-malware-rises-deceptive-apps-use-signed-binaries-and-seo-poisoning-to-hijack-browsers/ • https://www.acronis.com/en/tru/posts/cooking-up-trouble-how-tamperedchef-uses-signed-apps-to-deliver-stealthy-payloads/ • https://www.sophos.com/en-us/blog/tamperedchef-serves-bad-ads-with-infostealers-as-the-main-course
ATT&CKT1053.005 T1059.007 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate enterprise software using XML-defined scheduled tasks installed from %TEMP% during MSI rollout — exclude by SCCM/Intune deployer parent
  • Backup or update agents creating recurring JS-driven tasks (rare; verify product name is not on UC1 publisher list)
  • Developer running schtasks /create /xml against a local task.xml during testing — exclude by user/device dev-group
  • NodeJS/Electron app legitimately running .js with a productivity-themed name from %AppData% — verify signer
Suppression filter
and not (SchedParent in~ ("ccmexec.exe","TiWorker.exe","msiexec.exe") and SchedParentCompany has "Microsoft")
Response runbook
Triage: read the dropped task.xml (DeviceFileEvents query for the file) and inspect its <Actions> block — the malicious tasks call wscript/cscript on a JS file under the app's install dir or %AppData%. Confirm publisher matches UC1's shell-company list. Contain: delete the scheduled task (`schtasks /delete /tn <name>`), kill the running script host, isolate the host, rotate browser credentials. Hunt: pull DeviceFileEvents for all .xml task files dropped by the same parent process across the fleet and dump the corresponding .js bodies; pivot DeviceImageLoadEvents on the script host PIDs to surface any in-memory follow-on stealer modules. Run UC2 to find prior dormant C2 callbacks on each affected host.
let WindowHours = 24h;
let ScheduleHits = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName =~ "schtasks.exe"
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_all ("/create","/xml")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\","AppSuite","CrystalPDF","Calendaromatic","JustAskJacky","task.xml")
  | project SchedTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
            SchedCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
            SchedParent = InitiatingProcessFileName,
            SchedParentCompany = InitiatingProcessVersionInfoCompanyName;
let ScriptHits = DeviceProcessEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where FileName in~ ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe","node.exe")
  | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("appsuite-print.js","appsuite","crystalpdf","calendaromatic","justaskjacky") and ProcessCommandLine has ".js"
  | project ScriptTime = Timestamp, DeviceName, ScriptCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
            ScriptParent = InitiatingProcessFileName;
ScheduleHits
| join kind=inner ScriptHits on DeviceName
| where ScriptTime between (SchedTime .. SchedTime + WindowHours)
| project SchedTime, ScriptTime, DeviceName, AccountName,
          SchedParent, SchedParentCompany, SchedCmd,
          ScriptParent, ScriptCmd
| order by SchedTime desc
let WindowHours = 24h;
let ScheduleHits = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName endswith "schtasks.exe"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("/create","/xml")
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\","AppSuite","CrystalPDF","Calendaromatic","JustAskJacky","task.xml")
  | project SchedTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
            SchedCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
            SchedParentName = ParentProcessName,
            SchedParentCompany = ParentProcessFileCompany;
let ScriptHits = ImProcessCreate
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where ActingProcessName endswith "wscript.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "cscript.exe" or ActingProcessName endswith "node.exe"
  | where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("appsuite-print.js","appsuite","crystalpdf","calendaromatic","justaskjacky") and ActingProcessCommandLine has ".js"
  | project ScriptTime = TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ScriptCmd = ActingProcessCommandLine,
            ScriptParent = ParentProcessName;
ScheduleHits
| join kind=inner ScriptHits on DvcHostname
| where ScriptTime between (SchedTime .. SchedTime + WindowHours)
| project SchedTime, ScriptTime, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          SchedParentName, SchedParentCompany, SchedCmd,
          ScriptParent, ScriptCmd
| order by SchedTime desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\\schtasks.exe OR *\\SCHTASKS.EXE)) @CommandLine:(*"/create"* AND *"/xml"*) (@CommandLine:*task.xml* OR @CommandLine:*AppSuite* OR @CommandLine:*CrystalPDF* OR @CommandLine:*Calendaromatic* OR @CommandLine:*JustAskJacky* OR @CommandLine:*appsuite-print.js*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/\\schtasks\.exe$/i
| regex("/create", field=CommandLine)
| regex("/xml", field=CommandLine)
| regex("(task\\.xml|AppSuite|CrystalPDF|Calendaromatic|JustAskJacky|appsuite-print\\.js)", field=CommandLine)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" Processes.process="*/create*" Processes.process="*/xml*" (Processes.process LIKE "%\\Temp\\%task.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%\\AppData\\%task.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%AppSuite%task%.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%CrystalPDF%task%.xml%") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@d") | join type=outer dest [| tstats summariesonly=true count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") (Processes.process LIKE "%appsuite-print.js%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%appsuite%.js%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%crystalpdf%.js%") by Processes.dest Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename process as script_cmdline]
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmdline values(Processes.parent_process_name) as parent from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name="schtasks.exe" Processes.process="*/create*" Processes.process="*/xml*" (Processes.process LIKE "%\\Temp\\%task.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%\\AppData\\%task.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%AppSuite%task%.xml%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%CrystalPDF%task%.xml%") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where firstTime >= relative_time(now(), "-30d@d") | join type=outer dest [| tstats summariesonly=false count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.process_name IN ("wscript.exe","cscript.exe") (Processes.process LIKE "%appsuite-print.js%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%appsuite%.js%" OR Processes.process LIKE "%crystalpdf%.js%") by Processes.dest Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | rename process as script_cmdline]
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("crystalpdf.com", "vault.appsuites.ai", "pdf-tool.appsuites.ai", "appsuites.ai", "freeonlinetools.info")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,

let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["crystalpdf.com", "vault.appsuites.ai", "pdf-tool.appsuites.ai", "appsuites.ai", "freeonlinetools.info"]);
ImNetworkSession

title: Browser Extension Installation via Registry
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d0a
status: experimental
description: |

    administrative install of an extension. Often used by adware /

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] DNS / Network egress to TeamPCP Nx Console C2 domain check.git-service.com · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Burst credential-file harvest by VS Code / node process (Nx Console stealer behaviour) · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
DNS / Network egress to TeamPCP Nx Console C2 domain check.git-service.com AICommand & Control High
Hunts any developer endpoint resolving or connecting to check.git-service.com (or sibling subdomains under git-service.com), the credential-exfiltration host used by the TeamPCP Nx Console v18.95.0 supply-chain payload. The domain has no legitimate use — any hit is high-fidelity for the GitHub-breach campaign. Rationale: Domain check.git-service.com is the article's lead IOC; cross-checked via BleepingComputer and StepSecurity write-ups of the same Nx Console v18.95.0 / TeamPCP incident. Any DNS query for this name from a corporate endpoint indicates active credential exfiltration in progress. Cross-checked against: • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/github-confirms-breach-of-3-800-repos-via-malicious-vscode-extension/ • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://thehackernews.com/2026/05/github-internal-repositories-breached.html
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Network_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SOC analyst triaging the IOC from a jump host (curl/dig/nslookup against the indicator)
  • IOC enrichment tooling (MISP, OpenCTI, TheHive) auto-resolving the domain for context
  • VirusTotal sandbox detonation traffic if VT IDS feed is ingested into the same DNS lake
  • Threat-intel vendor periodic re-resolution of historic IOCs
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl.exe","nslookup.exe","dig.exe","powershell.exe") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("misp","opencti","thehive","virustotal","--ioc"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: confirm which user, process, and parent process initiated the egress (InitiatingProcessFileName / ContextImageFileName). If Code.exe, node.exe, or npx is in the chain treat as confirmed Nx Console infection on the workstation. 2. Contain: isolate the device via Defender LiveResponse / CS Network Containment, force-rotate every GitHub PAT, npm token, AWS access key, 1Password recovery key, and HashiCorp Vault token bound to that user identity; revoke all GitHub SSH/OAuth grants for the user; invalidate active SSO sessions. 3. Hunt: pivot on AccountName/UserName across the last 30 days for additional egress to git-service.com siblings, recent `git clone` of internal repos from the user's PAT, and any new orphan-commit pushes the stolen token may have made.

TeamPCP Nx Console payload SHA256 hash match on developer endpoints AIInstallation Medium
Direct hash-based detection for the four known Nx Console v18.95.0 malicious payload SHA256s — the 2,777-byte injected stub plus the dropped 498KB obfuscated stealer fetched from the nrwl/nx orphan commit. Any write or execution of these binaries on a corporate endpoint is unambiguous compromise. Rationale: Four SHA256s from the article's IOC block; campaign and payload behaviour cross-checked against the official nrwl/nx-console GHSA advisory and StepSecurity analysis. Hash matches on developer endpoints are unambiguous and warrant immediate isolation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/nrwl/nx-console/security/advisories/GHSA-c9j4-9m59-847w • https://www.stepsecurity.io/blog/nx-console-vs-code-extension-compromised • https://nx.dev/blog/nx-console-v18-95-0-postmortem
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1059.006 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Endpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Malware-analysis sandbox / detonation VM intentionally executing the known sample
  • Endpoint AV/EDR vendor lab machine running the sample for signature tuning
  • SOC reverse-engineering workstation handling the dropped 498KB stealer for IR analysis
  • Aikido / StepSecurity / similar SCA tool quarantining the sample in a controlled location
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in~ ("malware-sandbox-01","ir-analysis-vm","av-lab-01")
Response runbook
1. Triage: identify the user, parent VS Code process, and timestamp of first hash hit; check whether the device is a sandbox/RE box (allowlist if confirmed). 2. Contain: isolate the host immediately, capture memory if feasible, force rotation of all developer credentials (GitHub PAT, npm token, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.npmrc, ~/.kube/config, ~/.claude/settings.json, 1Password recovery key, HashiCorp Vault tokens) bound to the user, revoke all GitHub OAuth grants and active SSO sessions for that identity. 3. Hunt: pivot the SHA256 fleet-wide for prior sightings, search VS Code extension install telemetry for nrwl.angular-console v18.94.x / v18.95.0, audit GitHub Enterprise audit log for unusual `repo:clone` events from the user's PAT in the prior 30 days.
